Bacterial Spot.description: A bacterial disease that attacks leaves, stems and fruit.
Bacterial Spot.symptoms: Small dark, water-soaked spots on leaves; spots turn brown with a yellow halo; curled and yellowing leaves.
Bacterial Spot.treatment: Remove badly infected plants, water from the base (avoid wetting leaves), rotate crops, and use certified disease-free seeds.

Early blight.description: A fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani, common in warm and humid weather.
Early blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target-like) on lower leaves; yellowing and leaf drop.
Early blight.treatment: Remove infected leaves, improve air flow between plants, mulch the soil, and water early in the day so leaves dry quickly.

Late Blight.description: A serious fungal disease caused by Phytophthora infestans that spreads very quickly in wet weather.
Late Blight.symptoms: Large greasy-looking dark blotches on leaves and stems; white mold on the underside of leaves; rotting fruit.
Late Blight.treatment: Remove and burn infected plants, avoid overhead watering, keep the foliage dry, and do not compost infected material.

Leaf Mold.description: A fungal disease (Passalora fulva) that develops in warm, humid greenhouses.
Leaf Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow spots on upper leaves; olive-green to brown fuzzy mold on leaf undersides.
Leaf Mold.treatment: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity, water early in the day, and remove infected lower leaves.

Healthy.description: The plant shows no visible signs of disease.
Healthy.symptoms: None - the leaves are a uniform green without spots, discoloration or wilting.
Healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Continue normal care: regular watering, sunlight and balanced fertilizer.

Potato___Early_blight.description: A common fungal disease of potatoes caused by Alternaria solani.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves; yellowing leaves around the spots.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove infected foliage, avoid overhead watering, rotate potatoes with other crops, and remove plant debris after harvest.

Potato___Late_blight.description: The fungal disease (Phytophthora infestans) that caused the Irish potato famine.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked blotches on leaves and stems; white mold on leaf undersides; decayed tubers.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove infected plants immediately, destroy plant debris, avoid wet foliage, and store harvested potatoes in a cool dry place.

Potato___healthy.description: The plant shows no visible signs of disease.
Potato___healthy.symptoms: None - the leaves are a uniform green without spots, discoloration or wilting.
Potato___healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Continue normal care: regular watering, sunlight and balanced fertilizer.

Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease affecting pepper leaves and fruit, spread by water splash.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark spots on leaves that later turn brown; spots on fruit and leaf drop.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove infected plants, water at the base, rotate crops, and avoid working in the field when plants are wet.
